title: Start here
intro: Four albums that show the range: the blues weight of the early records, the acoustic side and the long epics.

stops.why: The best known of the lot, and the widest spread in one place: hard rock, folk, blues and the eight-minute centrepiece.
Written and recorded on the road in 1969. Riffs first, songs built around them.
A double album that covers everything they did, with Kashmir at its centre.
Brighter and more varied, with longer arrangements and more keyboards.

title: The blues roots
intro: They began as a heavy blues band. These records lean on Chicago and Delta blues, some of it credited to its writers only after later legal disputes.

stops.why: Made in a few days in late 1968. Two Willie Dixon songs and a long slow blues sit beside the originals.
Blues forms pushed louder and harder.
The slowest, deepest blues they recorded in the studio.
The same songs on the radio in 1969, often stretched out and played differently.

title: The acoustic side
intro: From the third album on, acoustic guitars and mandolins were as much part of the sound as amplifiers. Many of these songs began in Wales.

stops.why: The second side is almost all acoustic, written at a cottage in mid Wales.
Mandolin and a guest voice, Sandy Denny, on one song; a quiet one about California on another.
Songs that start acoustic and build.
try: Over the Hills and Far Away

stops.why: Short acoustic pieces among the long electric ones.

title: The long songs
intro: Pieces of eight minutes and more, built in sections, where the band stretched out in the studio as they did on stage.

stops.why: The earliest of their long pieces, and a stage favourite for a decade.
Two of their longest studio recordings.
Opens with a ten-minute song recorded fast in Munich.
Keyboard-led, and their last long piece.

title: Live Zeppelin
intro: On stage the songs changed every night. These releases cover the radio sessions, the 1972 and 1973 tours and the reunion.

stops.why: Radio sessions and concerts from 1969 and 1971.
Two California nights in June 1972, released in 2003.
Madison Square Garden, July 1973, from the concert film.
The only full show after 1980, at the O2 in December 2007.

title: The last chapter
intro: After Plant's car crash and before the end: harder, then lighter and more open to new sounds.

stops.why: Guitar-led, no keyboards, no acoustics; made quickly while Plant was recovering.
Recorded in Stockholm; Jones's keyboards shape the sound.
Leftovers from across their career, gathered after they split.
